segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [quiet underwater station ventilation hum] [softly] Close your eyes if comfortable and imagine resting inside a quiet station beneath a blue ocean. Nothing outside needs to vanish.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Hear the furthest sound as though it travels through water to reach you. Receive the vibration, then let it continue past.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice nearer sounds... the room... clothing... breathing. Each is a small instrument panel reporting that the world is still there.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Imagine one outer porthole becoming softly frosted. Sight grows less important for a while, without being forced away.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel temperature on the skin, then let attention sink beneath it toward pressure, weight, and the slow movement of the belly.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Taste and scent may be faint. Let those channels rest too, like underwater microphones placed on standby.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] The senses keep working; Pratyahara changes your relationship with their messages. You can hear a knock without opening every door.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Choose one inner sensation: heartbeat, breath, warmth, or the simple feeling of being contained by the body.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If an outer signal brightens, notice it and let it dim naturally. Return to the quiet pressure of the ocean around the station.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Rest in the inner room for several breaths. No perfect silence is necessary. Even the deep sea contains distant songs.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Begin clearing the portholes. Include sound, temperature, light behind the eyelids, and the shape of the whole body.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Move gently and open your eyes. Rise from the blue station slowly, keeping its quiet room somewhere within reach.
